answer: No. Your records show no blood clot in your lung. The scan you remember was a CT scan of your chest on 8 July 2025, done to check for a clot. Its report concludes: no pulmonary embolism, and the lungs are clear. A possible clot was written down that day, but it was later marked as ruled out. The scan was ordered because a blood test called D-dimer came back high that day (0.92, where the normal limit is 0.49). A high D-dimer alone does not mean there is a clot, because it rises for many reasons, so the scan was the way to check. You also had chest wall pain around that time, and the record shows it had settled by 22 July 2025. If you get new chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling, get it checked promptly.
short: No blood clot in the lung. A chest CT on 8 July 2025 showed no pulmonary embolism, and the clot entry from that day is marked refuted. A high D-dimer blood test prompted the scan.

knowledge.says: D-dimer is very sensitive but not specific. It rises with infection, inflammation, surgery, pregnancy and many other conditions, so a raised level on its own does not confirm a clot. That is why it is used to decide whether imaging is needed.
